verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Disdain and get thrown into his Purge/passive flames before Q is up; you win every extended trade and every stage after you've stacked a few minion kills on E.

brief.thesis: Sion's 54% win rate over 87 games comes from out-sustaining Urgot's ranged poke, not out-trading it directly: Grasp of the Undying and E (Enrage)'s permanent max-HP growth turn his auto-reliant chip damage into a losing war of attrition. Urgot's actual leverage is E (Disdain, 475 range, 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s cooldown) — a dash that shields him and throws the first champion it hits out of position, which is exactly how he gets his solo kills; it also beats a committed Q (550 range, point-and-click stun) because Disdain has mobility and a shield where Q has neither.

theirWindow.when: Disdain is up and you're near minions
theirWindow.what: He can dash through the wave, catch you, and throw you back toward his side of the lane — don't stand in a line he can path through, and don't commit Q first since Disdain beats it.

yourWindow.what: He has no shield and no escape. Toggle E (Enrage), close with Q for the stun, and commit — this is the only time an all-in is safe before level 6.

start.why: 54.6%-plus relevant pick rate (55.4% WR, 64.9% pick) and its passive negates exactly the kind of small-hit poke Urgot's autos and passive flame procs deal.

boots.why: 56.1% win rate over 82 games; flat damage reduction on autos directly cuts Urgot's Echoing Flames and basic-attack poke, which is his main damage source before 6.

core.why: stacks HP from proc'd damage, compounding with E's permanent max-HP growth to out-scale his DPS.
the omnivamp and shield let you facetank his auto-reliant damage profile while you look for all-in windows.

runes.keystoneWhy: per-trade healing neutralizes his ranged poke damage and the bonus HP stacks directly with E's permanent max-HP growth from minion kills.

summoners.why: 91.2% pick rate at 55.3% win rate; Teleport lets you reset the wave instead of fighting through his levels 3-5 poke advantage and arrive scaled for the levels where you actually win trades.

playing.title: Don't toggle E for free
playing.detail: Enrage costs health per attack with zero cooldown to turn off, so only hold it active when you're actually committing to a trade or a last-hit — not while eating his poke for nothing.

playing.title: Never Q first into Disdain range
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read is correct: Urgot's E beats your Q because it has a shield and mobility where your stun has neither. Wait for his Disdain to be spent or bait it out before you commit.

playing.title: All-in only when Disdain is down
playing.detail: The 14-16s window where he has no shield and no escape is your only safe all-in before level 6. Track it like a cooldown, not a guess.

playing.title: Detonate W into his Purge channel
playing.detail: Death's Caress's shield absorbs the Corrosive Charge explosion and auto-attack chip; pop it early for the AoE damage if he's channeling Purge next to you.

playing.title: Respect R range even off-screen
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death has 2500 range and executes below a health threshold — don't walk around at low HP anywhere near his line of sight after level 6.

playing.title: Use R to win extended skirmishes
playing.detail: Cannibalism's leech and attack speed are strongest in the long trades Grasp and E set up — save it for the all-in, not for poke exchanges.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid his (E) and (P). Use [Q] carefully as his (E) has the upper hand.
